title: Spectral Feedback for Test-Time Alignment of Protein Diffusion Models
claim: Wrapping an off-the-shelf generative model in a feedback loop that selects which tokens to revisit lets it iteratively correct its own outputs.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, teal feedback arrow looping over top, dashed init path below
description: A single horizontal block diagram. On the far left is a column of six white cells, all labeled M (masked tokens). An arrow leads into a large dark-teal box labeled 'Spectral Feedback', which is the first thing the eye lands on. From it, an arrow goes to a partially masked sequence of colored cells: T, M, V, M, M, C. That sequence feeds a beige box labeled 'Off-the-Shelf Protein Diffusion Model', and an arrow leads from that box to a fully unmasked sequence of colored cells: T, G, V, A, L, C. A solid teal arrow runs from the top of the output column back to the Spectral Feedback box, closing the loop. A dashed brown path labeled 'Initialize' runs from the all-masked column along the bottom up into the diffusion model. A dashed arrow labeled 'Final Output' leaves the output column downward.
caption: Spectral Feedback loop using targeted edits to iteratively improve attributes of a protein sequence with discrete diffusion.
abstract: Discrete diffusion models have become leading architectures for inverse protein folding. Test-time alignment guides these models during inference to generate proteins with desirable attributes. Alignment methods for discrete diffusion models often treat inference as a unidirectional process, lacking effective mechanisms for revisiting undesirable token selections. We introduce Spectral Feedback, an algorithm that selects edit-positions in a feedback loop, allowing the model to iteratively correct its own generations. This approach leverages the masking structure of discrete diffusion models by re-masking and re-sampling tokens. While prior alignment methods focus on what token labels to assign to maximize a target reward, we instead treat which tokens to revisit as the central alignment problem. Selecting edit-positions is challenging because edit effects are interdependent: the impact of modifying one token depends on which others are edited simultaneously. We define an edit-set as a set of positions to edit by re-masking and re-sampling the corresponding tokens in a sequence. Motivated by prior work on sparse interactions in biological systems, we find empirically that edit-set value functions for protein inverse folding admit sparse Fourier representations. This structure enables Spectral Feedback to efficiently learn and optimize the value functions for edit-position selection. Spectral Feedback is model-agnostic and can be applied to pre-trained, test-time aligned, and fine-tuned diffusion models without modifying the underlying generative processes. Applied to inverse folding with a protein stability reward oracle, Spectral Feedback increases the proportion of stable proteins by 32.3 percentage points over a pre-trained model, 24.8 over Best-of-10, and 5.8 over a state-of-the-art RL fine-tuned diffusion model.
